item.title: In India, tainted alcohol leaves 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised
item.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. item.title: Major regional sports law body to set up Hong Kong base by year end: minister
item.description: A major regional sports law organisation will establish its headquarters in Hong Kong by the end of the year, the city’s deputy justice minister has said, while a lawmaker has suggested more sports bodies will set up bases in the city “as part of a continuing wave”. item.title: Sun-dried yoghurt, floor dining: how migration, folding chairs reshaped Chinese food
item.description: With a history as long as China’s, some cultural traditions are bound to fade into antiquity. This is especially true of food, which can change dramatically within a single lifetime. Some changes are fundamental, making it almost impossible to imagine the culture without them; others are quirks of history. item.title: Hong Kong will not rule out whistle-blower immunity in bid-rigging law: minister
item.description: Hong Kong authorities will not rule out the inclusion of immunity provisions for whistle-blowers in proposed legal amendments to outlaw bid-rigging in building maintenance and renovation projects, the commerce chief has said. Officials vowed to amend the law after an independent committee identified bid-rigging as one of the causes behind the Tai Po fire in November 2025 that claimed 168 lives and displaced almost 5,000 people. item.title: China has real economic troubles, ‘Japanification’ not among them
item.description: If one manifestation of the economic difficulties Japan faced from the 1990s was falling inflation and bond yields, then China is falling into the same malaise. Starting with longer maturities, interest rates on government debt in China have been falling below equivalents in Japan. The People’s Bank of China’s recent announcement of an overnight policy rate of 1.25 per cent brings the process close to completion.
